turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning, Mr Khumalo. Come through and sit. What has brought you in today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. My sugar has been sitting too high, and I felt it was time for a proper review.

[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I am the one who pushed him, doctor. He has been tired after work, falling asleep in the chair. And the parking here is a nightmare, hey, we went round the block twice.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): That is fair, about the tiredness. I have been weary. I did not wish to waste a consultation on it.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): It is not a waste. How long have you had the type 2 diabetes, and what are you actually taking for it?

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): It will be eight years in November, doctor. I take metformin tablets by mouth, one gram in the morning and one gram at night. And the night-time insulin, Lantus, eighteen units, which I inject.
[SEG0007] person_4 (NURSE): Sorry, doctor, may I come in there. The chemist script in the file, from March, has insulin glargine, the Lantus, at twenty-four units at night, not eighteen.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I was quite sure it was eighteen, sister. Well, actually, that is what I dial on the pen. I have always believed it was eighteen.

[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me say that back so I have it straight. You dial eighteen units, and Sister has a March script for twenty-four units of the same Lantus. I am not going to treat those as the same figure.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you inject it every night, or are there nights it does not happen?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I must be honest with you. On work days I often skip it. I leave at five for the deliveries and, um, the pen stays in the fridge.
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, weekends he does take it. Monday to Friday, half the time it is still sitting there when I get in.

[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): All right. Thinking it through, the high readings could be the missed doses, or this eighteen-versus-twenty-four mix-up, or what you eat out on the road. I am not going to pin it on a single cause yet.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand, doctor. I am sorry about the missed doses. It is not how I was brought up to treat a prescription.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): When you do check at home, what sort of fasting numbers have you been seeing?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): The fasting one is one-eighty-something. Sometimes I look again and I think it said two hundred. The book is at home, and I do muddle the figures, I am afraid.

[SEG0017] person_4 (NURSE): The finger-prick here this morning was eleven point four millimoles per litre. Blood pressure one forty-six over eighty-eight millimetres of mercury, and the pulse was seventy-six beats a minute.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thank you, sister. Mr Khumalo, your feet. Any tingling, any open sores, any pain in them?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): There is a tingling in both feet, for about three months now. I have not seen any sores, and there is no real pain.
[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He did get a small blister from new work boots last month. It healed. There is nothing open on the feet now.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the eyes. Any blurring, any sudden loss of vision, and when were you last at the eye clinic?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): It goes a little blurry in the evenings, when I read. No sudden loss. The last eye check... well, I cannot tell you when. I simply do not remember.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines, or to anything else?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): None that I know of, doctor.

[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will look at the feet now. The skin is intact, and there is no ulcer on either foot. The pulses are present. Sensation with the monofilament is a bit dull on both soles.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): My first thought, I will say it plainly, was to increase the Lantus to twenty-eight units from tonight, and to send you for a foot X-ray because of that tingling.
[SEG0027] person_4 (NURSE): If he is already between eighteen and twenty-four, and skipping the work nights, a jump to twenty-eight might be the wrong move, doctor.
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And he eats those garage pies on the route. I tell him, but there we are.

[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): You are right, sister. I am changing that plan. No increase today, and no foot X-ray. I will not write a new insulin dose until I have seen the box you actually use at home.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Should I carry on with eighteen, then, or should I move to the twenty-four?

[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): I cannot safely pick one from this chair. Bring the box and the script label next time. Please keep taking the metformin, one gram morning and night, which you manage more steadily.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. The metformin I take properly, both doses. It is only the insulin that gets left behind on work days.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): So my working impression is that the glucose is running high mainly because the night insulin is missed on work days. It is also possible the eighteen-versus-twenty-four mix-up is playing a part, and I cannot settle that today. I am not going to call this a foot infection.

[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): We will do an HbA1c today. I will also book the eye clinic for a retinal check, as we cannot date the last one. Come back in two weeks with the insulin box and the sugar book.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): I will do that. Is there anything I ought to change with food in the meantime, doctor?

[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. Try to leave the garage pies, and take a lunch from home. Do not skip the insulin just because the shift starts early. And check both feet each evening for any break in the skin.
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will pack the lunch. I can put the pen by the kettle so he sees it before he goes.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): That would help, thank you. I will make a proper effort not to miss it.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. Sister will take the HbA1c sample before you leave. We will look at it together in two weeks. There are no new tablets from me today.
[SEG0040] person_4 (NURSE): I will do the bloods at the next window, Mr Khumalo. It will not take long.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor, and thank you, sister. I do appreciate the time you have given me.
